questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: College hostel (twin share)

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Canteens and floor kitchen

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: All living options are shared rooms. International House (I-house) is where most exchange students live and other college halls have more local students.

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Very simple. OAL is the office responsible for all affairs related to exchange students and the staff are experienced and efficient.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Online consultation, online orientation, creating Facebook group ect.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I successfully registered in all classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
1. There will be a pre-selection for the school to check if you meet the course requirements. 
2. In the first two weeks, you are free to add/drop classes. 
3. There will be a waiting list if the quota is full.

questions.answer: There are many natural attractions in Hong Kong and countless hiking trails with amazing ocean views.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy for me (as a Chinese) and as far as I know from other European exchange students, it was not challenging.

questions.answer: Having a local roommate (you can put it on the living preferences list)

questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
The mix of traditional Chinese and Western culture in every way: food, architecture,
lifestyles...very
inclusive.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. It has the most beautiful and big campus in Hong Kong - built on a mountain, with a harbour view and has many wild plants and animals (monkey, boar, snake...) It's easy to get lost.
2. Exchange can only choose courses taught in English but Chinese language courses are available. Also, CUHK has one of the best China studies centres in the world.
3. The campus is a bit far from the city centre (and nightlife) but has everything daily needed nearby.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The weather is very different from Denmark. Summer is extremely humid and hot while winter is pleasant. Cycling is not very common.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Friendships and nature exploration.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: One of the courses was a bit overloaded with many homework to do.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
